canonical_statement: The trial prospectively compared acalabrutinib with ibrutinib in previously treated CLL to test whether acalabrutinib was noninferior for progression-free survival with improved tolerability.
Eligible patients were at least 18 years old, had previously treated CLL requiring therapy, ECOG performance status 0-2, and centrally confirmed del(17)(p13.1) and/or del(11)(q22.3).

population.label: Eligibility population
inclusion_criteria: therapy required by International Workshop on CLL criteria
central confirmation of del(17)(p13.1) and/or del(11)(q22.3)

canonical_statement: Patients were excluded for significant cardiovascular disease, concomitant warfarin or equivalent vitamin K antagonist treatment, prior BTK or BCL-2 inhibitor treatment, or a requirement for proton-pump inhibitor treatment.

population.label: Eligibility population
exclusion_criteria: concomitant warfarin or equivalent vitamin K antagonist treatment

canonical_statement: Acalabrutinib was administered orally at 100 mg twice daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

exposures.duration: until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

canonical_statement: Ibrutinib was administered orally at 420 mg once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

exposures.duration: until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

canonical_statement: The study was a phase III randomized multicenter open-label noninferiority trial (NCT02477696).

Eligible patients were randomly assigned 1:1; randomization was stratified by del(17)(p13.1) status, ECOG performance status (2 vs ≤1), and number of prior therapies (1-3 vs ≥4), and crossover was not permitted.
An independent review committee assessed progression and response data centrally in a blinded manner, while the treatment assignment itself was open label.
The primary endpoint was independent review committee-assessed progression-free survival, defined as time from random assignment to disease progression or death from any cause.

outcome.definition: Time from random assignment until disease progression or death from any cause
outcome.measurement_method: International Workshop on CLL 2008 response criteria

canonical_statement: Secondary endpoints were any-grade atrial fibrillation, grade 3 or higher infections, Richter transformation, and overall survival.

outcome.definition: Any-grade atrial fibrillation; grade ≥3 infections; Richter transformation; overall survival

canonical_statement: The noninferiority design used an acalabrutinib-to-ibrutinib hazard-ratio margin of 1.429 (30% margin); 500 patients were planned to provide 80% power at a one-sided 0.025 significance level.

After establishing PFS noninferiority, superiority testing was gate-kept in sequence for any-grade atrial fibrillation, grade ≥3 infections, Richter transformation, and overall survival; once a superiority test failed, subsequent P values were descriptive.
Efficacy analyses used the intention-to-treat population; safety analyses used all patients who received at least one dose of study drug.
Of 808 screened patients, 533 were randomly assigned at 124 centers in 15 countries: 268 to acalabrutinib and 265 to ibrutinib.

population.label: Previously treated CLL with centrally confirmed del(17)(p13.1) and/or del(11)(q22.3); intention-to-treat population

canonical_statement: The overall median age was 66 years (range 28-89 years).
At baseline, 241 of 533 patients (45.2%) had del(17)(p13.1) and 342 of 533 (64.2%) had del(11)(q22.3).
The median number of prior therapies was two in both treatment arms, with an overall range of 1-12.
Men comprised 185 of 268 (69.0%) acalabrutinib patients and 194 of 265 (73.2%) ibrutinib patients.
ECOG performance status 0-1 was present in 247 of 268 (92.2%) acalabrutinib patients and 243 of 265 (91.7%) ibrutinib patients.
Chromosome 17p13.1 deletion was present in 121 of 268 (45.1%) acalabrutinib patients and 120 of 265 (45.3%) ibrutinib patients.
Chromosome 11q22.3 deletion was present in 167 of 268 (62.3%) acalabrutinib patients and 175 of 265 (66.0%) ibrutinib patients.
TP53 mutation was present in 100 of 268 (37.3%) acalabrutinib patients and 112 of 265 (42.3%) ibrutinib patients.
Unmutated IGHV was present in 220 of 268 (82.1%) acalabrutinib patients and 237 of 265 (89.4%) ibrutinib patients.
Complex karyotype was present in 124 of 268 (46.3%) acalabrutinib patients and 125 of 265 (47.2%) ibrutinib patients.

After median follow-up of 40.9 months, median IRC-assessed PFS was 38.4 months in both arms; the acalabrutinib-to-ibrutinib HR was 1.00 (95% CI 0.79-1.27), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion.

canonical_statement: The PFS Kaplan-Meier curves crossed at approximately 33 months, violating the proportional-hazards assumption; the authors therefore reported an RMST sensitivity analysis.
The trial was open label, so patients and treating physicians knew treatment assignment, although the independent review committee was blinded.
The study population was restricted to previously treated CLL with del(17)(p13.1) and/or del(11)(q22.3), limiting direct generalization beyond this higher-risk population.
Survival outcomes were not analyzed by cause of treatment discontinuation, so the study did not determine whether differences in adverse-event discontinuations affected survival.

The authors concluded that acalabrutinib was noninferior to ibrutinib for PFS and had improved safety with fewer atrial fibrillation events and fewer treatment discontinuations because of adverse events.
The authors interpreted the trial as showing similar efficacy but better tolerability for acalabrutinib than ibrutinib in previously treated CLL.

Multiple authors reported financial relationships with Acerta Pharma/AstraZeneca and other pharmaceutical companies; several coauthors were employees of Acerta Pharma or AstraZeneca.
